data.source_text_main_point: Police raided The Pirate Bay and Piratbyrån servers on copyright violation grounds, but while authorities claim no arrests occurred, operators and a detained web host allege the move was a politically motivated sting by the Anti-Piracy Bureau to shut down the site and seize unrelated servers without legal basis.

actors.name: Rickard Falkvinge
variations: head of the Swedish Pirate Party

actors.name: Dan Glickman
variations: CEO of the Motion Picture Association of America

statements.key_statement: The raid on the site based on alleged copyright violations was surprising given the long-standing public legal debate.
statements.long_statement: A search warrant was executed to close the site for suspected copyright infringement. This action was unexpected, given that the operation's legality had been heavily debated by the public for more than three years. During this time, the operators often released press statements to support their stance.

statements.key_statement: Rickard Falkvinge stated that law enforcement detained three employees, but only two individuals were actually placed in custody.
statements.long_statement: Rickard Falkvinge, who leads the Swedish Pirate Party, stated that law enforcement detained three employees of the website. However, only two people were actually placed in custody. This difference conflicts with the official police report on how many arrests occurred.

statements.key_statement: Dan Glickman praised the police action against The Pirate Bay, noting it shows that copyright thieves have no safe havens.
statements.long_statement: Dan Glickman, who leads the Motion Picture Association of America, praised the police operation against The Pirate Bay. He stated that this raid serves as a vital warning: copyright infringers have no safe havens. He also stressed that digital platforms must be held responsible for sharing illegal material.

statements.key_statement: Official confirmation of the raid contrasts with a detained host's account of being denied legal representation.
statements.long_statement: Swedish officials have confirmed the authenticity of the police raid on The Pirate Bay, a move that aligns with the site's own updated notice promising a quick return, even as a detained web host alleges he was arrested and denied legal representation during the operation.

statements.key_statement: Swedish police denied a detained web host a public defender by citing the non-custodial nature of his specific charge.
statements.long_statement: The Swedish National Criminal Police informed the detained web host, Gottfrid Svartholm, that he was not entitled to a public defender because the specific charge he faced did not carry a potential prison sentence, a legal justification used to deny him legal representation during the interrogation phase of the raid on The Pirate Bay and associated servers.
